title: One address, five landlords
lede: The original Atari was gone a decade before the web. What atari.com shows instead is the afterlife: each capture below belongs to a different owner or strategy. These are screenshots of pages saved by the Internet Archive’s Wayback Machine, found in October 2026. Click one to open the original capture.[^32]

snips.text: “Join the Alpha Web Site and help create a legend. Play, Live & Create”

note: We could not get a usable capture from the Hasbro years. In the captures we tried from 1999 to early 2001 the address returned a few hundred bytes or forwarded to hasbrointeractive.com/atari, where the archived page is an error. Images are missing from several captures; the screenshots show them as archived.

captures.label: JTS era
captures.title: “Jagwire”
captures.text: Five weeks before the sale to Hasbro. The front page still promotes the Jaguar console’s “Interactive Multimedia Domain” and carries the line “A JTS Corporation subsidiary.” JTS made disk drives.[^13]

captures.label: Infogrames era
captures.title: “Infogrames is now officially Atari”
captures.text: Five months after the U.S. company changed its name.[^16] The page is a list of country sites, with a note about the parent, Infogrames Entertainment SA.

captures.label: Before the buyout
captures.title: A portal, and an earnings call
captures.text: A region selector with links to Atari, Inc. and Infogrames investor relations. Atari, Inc.’s publishing revenue had fallen from $289.6M in fiscal 2005 to $104.7M in fiscal 2007.[^17]
captures.warn: Some images are missing from the capture.

captures.label: Publisher
captures.title: Star Trek Online, and Asteroids in a browser
captures.text: A conventional game publisher’s front page. The list on the left offers the 1980s arcade games Asteroids Deluxe, Battlezone and Gravitar to play online.
captures.warn: Some images are missing from the capture.

captures.label: Retro hardware
captures.title: A store
captures.text: A shop selling hardware, games and apparel. The pop-up shows a new wood-grain cartridge console beside boxed games. Hardware was €4.0M of the €33.6M of revenue in the year to March 2025.[^21]
